body:
- `global_wind_driven_gyres.jl` read ETOPO1 from NOAA's OPeNDAP servers, which fail intermittently and broke the docs build on 1cec629d3. It now downloads ETOPO1 sampled every 10 arc-minutes (4.5 MB) from OceananigansArtifacts.jl (glwagner/OceananigansArtifacts.jl#9) and averages it in blocks of `6resolution` samples, which also covers the ½° and 2° runs. An alternative is `DataDeps`, as the tests and validation scripts use, at the cost of adding a dependency to the docs environment.
- `@nolebase/vitepress-plugin-enhanced-readabilities` and `@nolebase/ui` 2.21.0 (published 2026-10-13) require VitePress 2, so `npm install` fails with `ERESOLVE` against our `vitepress@^1.6.3` and every docs build fails at the render step. Both are pinned to `~2.18.2`, whose peer range includes VitePress 1.

body:
SplitRungeKutta always restart from cached fields at the beginning of the time-step. However, when applying the deferred free surface for the implicit drag trick, we were using the stage free surface instead of the beginning-of-step-surface.
This lowers the order of the implicit drag and it makes it less effective. This PR fixes the implementation.
title: Correct implicit drag for split-RK

body:
Motivation for this was to make work some tests that were only commented out (added in #2881), spotted by @tomchor at https://github.com/CliMA/Oceananigans.jl/pull/6133#discussion_r4172462533.

> `regrid_in_x!` and `regrid_in_y!` weighted each source cell by its full
> horizontal area and divided by the area of the target cell.  This is only
> correct when source and target cells have the same extent in the other
> horizontal direction.  Regridding a field reduced over `y` and `z`, which
> lives on the full 3D grid, onto a 1D grid that is `Flat` in `y` scaled the
> contributions of partially overlapping source cells by the `Δy` of the
> source grid, giving wrong values in the target cells that straddle two
> source cells.
> 
> On `RectilinearGrid` and `LatitudeLongitudeGrid` the horizontal cell area
> factorizes into a factor depending only on `x` (`Δx` or `Δλ`) and one
> depending only on `y` (`Δy` or `Δsinφ`), so weight cells by their measure
> in the regridded direction only, as `regrid_in_z!` already does with `Δz`.
> This is exact for both grids and removes the need for
> `fractional_horizontal_area` and for the face counts passed to the kernels.
> 
> Re-enable the commented-out test that regrids a reduced field, which was
> disabled because of this problem and now passes in `x`, `y` and `z`.
title: Weight horizontal regridding by the length in the regridded direction

body:
The search-direction kernel reads ρ and ρⁱ⁻¹ and writes p = z + βp over the interior, and the update kernel computes α = ρ / pᵀq itself and stores ρ for the next iteration, so the three one-element broadcasts per iteration (β, α, ρⁱ⁻¹) and their host allocations are gone. Based on #6171.

64³ nonhydrostatic box, FFT-preconditioned CG with 7 iterations per solve, one H100, per step: 7.13–7.29 → 6.90–7.26 ms, launches 912 → 852, CUDA API calls 15.9k → 14.3k, host enqueue 7.8 → 7.5–7.7 ms. At 320×320×2560 with the Fourier-tridiagonal preconditioner the iteration is unchanged (155.0 → 154.8 ms). Matches the generic iteration to 1e-15 with identical iteration counts for no, FFT and diagonally dominant preconditioners.
